Gypsy's First Time Trying Out Her Wheelchair!

This is my SO and my GSD who was diagnosed with DM (degenerative myelopathy) as well as hip and spinal issues. She would have needed a total hip replacement and spinal surgery to enlarge some foramen to unpinch some nerves, but her DM diagnosis kept us from attempting to "fix" her as it was just a matter of time before it took her away from us. These pictures are 2 years old - we lost her a year ago to DM when it spread to her front legs, but I still miss her like it was only yesterday.

If anyone has any questions about living with a handicapped dog, how to maintain quality of life, daily challenges regarding their needs, and how doggy wheelchairs work, feel free to PM me. I have a short video of her using the wheelchair, too, if you're interested. The YouTube account shows my full name so I'm hesitant to put a link to it here - I may just reupload it to a different site and then share it that way.

[WP] You are a guard at a train station. One night, when nobody else is around, you are about to leave when you spot a guy getting ready to jump onto the tracks as a train is coming.

Don't do it. Don't you fucking dare. what a mess you will be. Those were my first thoughts when I saw the skittish, small man standing near the tracks, craning his neck, watching the far away train come closer; fast. I knew what he was about, had seen it before. Sure, I didn't want somebody to die, but I was angry, angry that he would subject others to his tragedy.

I started to run. I didn't want to yell, startle him, but I wasn't sure I was going to make it. I hadn't planned past tackling him, but I had to stop him from fucking up everyone's night, including his.

I was almost there, but so was the train. I was going to beat it. He saw me at the last second, jumped and ran towards the barreling machine. I felt the mist as the collision happened five feet away from my now frozen form.

Fuck.

It was my last day working the graveyard shift, I had just finished my degree and was a week away from my new position at a start up company. After tonight, I'm going back to the apartment, cracking open a 6 pack and completely checking out of reality.

I've been watching the bar rush stumble across the platform night after night and with the exception of the occasional lightweight losing their dinner, I haven't had much to complain about. But tonight, tonight was different. There was something particularly eerie in the air.

Maybe it was just my luck that something like this would happen on my last night but then again, who am I to believe in luck.

And there he stood, inches from the ledge, still as the night with a stare a million miles away. I'm not one to scare easily but his certainty sent the blood rushing to my feet.

Clumsily, I approach him and I wonder if he can hear my heart beating. When I reach him, I get a good look and I see that he's old. He has crowsfeet and wrinkles from laughter that was once alive. His hair is silver and his cologne reminded me of my own father.

"Sir.", I say. With my voice shaking, that was all that in could muster.

He turns to me and his eyes meet mine, the palest blue I've ever seen. He smiles with tears rolling down his cheeks and whispers, "Son", as he leaned foward into the tracks.

So, we've been growing as a sub quite steadily since the takeover, which is great.

However, with more content being submitted, most of which is great, I'm starting to notice a trend in a lot of content (sometimes links to the exact same content with only minor URL changes) being reposted.

I'm glad that everyone wants to submit content, but part of the problem is people are relying solely on the strict URL detection to tell them if content has already been posted.

I'd like to request, for the sake of quality in the sub, that people look on /v/mma/new before posting a link to ensure what they are about to post has not already been posted.

Up to this point, I have not been deleting the duplicate content, but if it continues to be a problem, I will have to start wiping out duplicates and keeping whatever link was posted first.

I don't blame anyone for the mixup, it's an easy thing to miss, but if you see that you post something and check /v/mma/new and you see it was already posted before you by someone else (except they used a shorter URL or https or whatever), please delete the duplicate content.

Also, to clarify, let's say someone has already posted an interview with McGregor hosted by mmafighting and then you post a link to the same interview from sherdog.... as long as there is content surrounding the interview, with different points of view etc. it's not really an issue, the problem is people posting links to the exact same content except one has been redirected through Facebook so it has a different URL or one is using the full youtube URL and the other is the shortened URL or the mobile URL.

The major issue is only when the content is the exact same thing, naturally we are going to have discussions and articles surrounding very similar content and that's not a problem.

I hope that clears it up and if anyone has a problem with this, please feel free to post here and we can figure it out.

Thanks!
